findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set explicitly and comments indicate it is public, with no public access block configuration to prevent public read/write access, exposing potentially sensitive customer data to the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket, including customer master data, are stored unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects (including customer-master.xlsx) cannot be recovered, compounding risk given the bucket is public.
No logging block is configured, so access to this public, unencrypted bucket containing sensitive data cannot be audited.

findings.issue_category: sensitive data exposure via public bucket
findings.description: This object (customer-master.xlsx, likely containing sensitive customer data) is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing the contents to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set for this financials bucket, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled on the financials bucket, risking permanent loss or undetected tampering of financial records.
No logging configuration is present for the financials bucket, preventing audit trails of access to sensitive financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the operations bucket, so stored data is unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for the operations bucket, preventing audit visibility into access of this data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for the data_science bucket, so stored data is unencrypted at rest despite having versioning and logging configured.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its (unencrypted, public) contents to be deleted without recovery safeguards, increasing risk of irreversible data loss especially combined with lack of versioning.
